entries.example: Right/OK, let's have a look at exercise 3.
Now, what shall we do next?
entries.group: Here are some common markers which organise the different stages of a conversation.

entries.example: So, would you like to come to the table now, please?
Good, I'll ring you on Thursday, then.
Well then, what was it you want to talk about?
Now then, I want you to look at this picture. [said by someone in control of the conversation, e.g. a teacher]
Fine/Great, let's leave it at that, then, shall we?
Mind you, it is November, so it's not surprising. [an afterthought, used like however]
Let me see, I have it here somewhere ... [a hesitation – gaining time]
Listen/Look, why don't you let me sort it out? [introducing a suggestion/point]
Hang on / Hold on! Let me tell you what he said! [preventing an interruption]
I can't do that. You see, I'm not the boss here. [explaining]
entries.group: Here are some other similar markers.

entries.example: He was, you know, sort of ... just standing there. [hesitation]
He was, you know, sort of ... just standing there. [hesitation]
So that's what we have to do. Anyway, I'll ring you tomorrow. [signalling that the speaker thinks the topic or the conversation can now close]
It rained all day yesterday. Still, we can't complain, it was fine all last week. [contrasts two ideas with one another]

entries.word: At the end of the day
entries.example: We shouldn't be too hard on him. At the end of the day, he's only a child. [the most important point or argument is ...]

note: Presentation is prose with bold discourse markers and printed bracket glosses rather than a table; no POS markers or IPA printed. Bracket glosses copied with examples as printed; some markers share one sentence (you know / sort of). Section-organising markers (Now, So, Good, etc.) listed under the printed sentence 'Here are some common markers...'; second set under 'Here are some other similar markers.'
